analysis: The code snippet contains two calls to `Thread.start()`: one on the outer thread created after `lockFile(port)`, and one on inner threads created within the outer thread’s run method. The outer thread is created once and started at the end of `startServer()`. The inner threads are created inside the `while` loop, each as a new `Thread` object. Since `start()` is called only once on each thread object (and the thread has not been started before), the condition for `IllegalThreadStateException` (starting an already started thread) is avoided in both contexts. No other exceptions are declared by `start()` according to the provided javadoc.
remark: IllegalThreadStateException is thrown when `start()` is called on a thread that has already been started. In this code, each thread (outer and inner) is a newly created object and `start()` is invoked exactly once on each, so the condition never occurs.
